titulo: A crack in America and the edge of the world
transcricao_contracapa:
"An absorbing narrative of the San Francisco earthquake of 1906 . . . a timely study of America's risky taste for civic culture on the edge of the abyss." The Independent.

In the early morning hours of April 18, 1906, an earthquake registering 8.25 on the Richter scale struck San Francisco and a string of towns to its north-northwest and south-southeast. The quake, lasting little more than a minute, toppled 25,000 buildings, broke open gas mains, and cut off electric power lines throughout the Bay area. Then came the fires that raged for three days, cutting a deadly 200-mile-long swath across coastal California, leaving chaos and horror in its wake while effectively destroying the gold rush capital that had stood for a half century. It was perhaps the worst natural disaster in the history of the United States.

Internationally bestselling author Simon Winchester vividly brings the cataclysm to life—offering a fascinating, in-depth exploration of a legendary event that changed the way we look at the planet on which we live.
sinopse: No dia 18 de abril de 1906, um terremoto de magnitude 8.25 atingiu San Francisco, causando a destruição de 25.000 edifícios e desativando o fornecimento de eletricidade. As chamas que se seguiram devastaram a Califórnia, resultando na pior catástrofe natural da história dos Estados Unidos. O autor Simon Winchester oferece uma análise profunda deste evento que transformou a cidade e alterou a percepção de como vemos nosso planeta.

conservacao.descricao_geral: Livro fisicamente bem conservado, porém fortemente amarelado. Texto livre de anotações e sublinhados. Não possui marcas de umidade, mofo ou traça.
